# Apply never completes on a fully valid quote — transient "employment details" error flashes and clears while the block persists

> **Status:** Draft · not yet filed in a tracker
> **Severity:** High — Apply is the core conversion action of this screen; if this is real
> and not environment-specific, no quote can proceed to the Apply Flow at all.
> **Component:** Quote › Illustration screen › Apply button / navigation
> **Environment:** `outsystems-dev.asteronlife.co.nz` (Asteron Connect Quote & Apply, "Illustration" step)
> **Found via:** Automated test (Playwright) — `apps/asteron-quote-apply/tests/quote-screen/validation-and-navigation.spec.js`
> (`VAL-08/VAL-09/VAL-10`, `VAL-11`) and `kids-cover.spec.js` (`KID-05`) — then live
> interactive follow-up with dedicated probes: `probe-triage-2026-08-26-failures.js`,
> `probe-val08-apply-silent-block.js`, `probe-val08-immediate-apply-check.js`,
> `probe-val08-income-hypothesis.js`
> **Reported:** 2026-08-26 · automated regression suite + live interactive follow-up

## Summary

Clicking **Apply** on what should be a fully valid, minimal single-Life quote (Age 35,
Gender Male, Occupation Code AA, Employment Status "Employed", Annual Income $150,000,
Life cover Sum Insured $200,000 — a config that prices successfully at $254.16/year, well
above the $240 minimum) does not complete. Per `VAL-08` in
`docs/confluence-pages/business-rules/quote-screen/validation-and-navigation/page.md`,
a successful Apply should replace the "Illustration" heading with a "Client summary"-style
heading and swap out the whole footer button set. Neither happens: the Apply button
remains present and enabled, the "Illustration" heading remains, and 8 seconds after the
click there is no stable visible error explaining why.

However, this is not simply "no error appears" — a genuine, specific error **does**
appear and then **disappears on its own**: *"Please complete the client's employment
details before applying"* (`VAL-23`) was observed present at ~620ms, ~1.6s, and ~3.6s
after the click, then gone by ~7.6s — on a quote where Employment Status genuinely had
been set to "Employed" beforehand. This looks like a real desync between the app's
validation-display layer (which shows, then clears, the error) and its actual validation
state (which apparently still blocks Apply) — not a test timing artifact. The same
"no stable error, Apply doesn't complete" pattern was also observed for `VAL-11`
(Employment Status deliberately left unset) and `KID-05` (a kid row with no Date of
Birth) — all three may share this same root mechanism.

## Preconditions

A logged-in adviser session, on a **fresh, unsaved quote** (`New Quote` from
`/QuoteAndApply/` → any adviser number). Age/Gender/Occupation Code/Employment
Status/Annual Income values used (35/Male/AA/Employed/$150,000) are all
**just-needs-to-be-valid**, not specific-and-required — re-tested with a completely
minimal baseline (no Employment Status, no Income at all) and got the identical result,
so this does not depend on the specific personal-details values chosen. Life cover with
Sum Insured $200,000 is **specific-and-required** only in the sense that *some* priced
cover above the $240/year minimum is needed to reach a state that should otherwise be
"fully valid" — the exact $200,000 figure isn't significant.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On the quote from the preconditions above, set Age Next Birthday = 35, Gender = Male,
   Occupation Code = AA.
2. Set Employment Status = "Employed" and Annual Income = $150,000 (or leave both unset —
   both were tested, same result).
3. Click **Life**, enter Sum Insured = $200,000, and wait for the premium to calculate
   (confirmed: $254.16/year in this run).
4. Click **Apply**.
5. Watch the page for at least 8 seconds without further interaction.
   - **Expected** (per `VAL-08`): the page transitions to a "Client summary"-style view —
     "Illustration" heading gone, footer buttons (Close/View PDF/Save as New/Save/Apply)
     replaced by different controls.
   - **Actual**: at ~0.6-3.6s, the error *"Please complete the client's employment details
     before applying"* is visible in the page text. By ~7.6s it is gone, but the page has
     NOT transitioned — "Illustration" heading still present, Apply button still present
     and enabled, no other visible error.

## Evidence

**Screenshot, ~8s after clicking Apply on the "fully valid" config (no error banner
visible, page otherwise looks completely normal):**

![Quote screen 8 seconds after clicking Apply on a fully valid config — no error, but no navigation either](data:image/png;base64,)

**Timed snapshots from a fresh, separate run (`probe-val08-immediate-apply-check.js`),
same config, confirming the transient message:**

| Time after click | Body text (truncated) |
|---|---|
| 620ms | *"Please complete the client's employment details before applying\n..."* |
| 1641ms | *(same message still present)* |
| 3644ms | *(same message still present)* |
| 7652ms | Message gone; page otherwise unchanged, still on Illustration |

Broader DOM search at the ~8s mark (`probe-val08-apply-silent-block.js`) found no modal,
no `aria-invalid` field, no `role="alert"`/`aria-live` content, and no red/highlighted
element — the block, whatever it is, produces no other visible signal once the transient
message clears:
```json
{
  "alerts": ["View PDF", "Apply"],
  "invalidFields": [],
  "redElements": [],
  "applyButtonPresent": true,
  "applyButtonDisabled": false,
  "hasIllustrationHeading": true,
  "modals": []
}
```

**Ruled out Annual Income as the real trigger** (`probe-val08-income-hypothesis.js`): a
config with Employment Status AND Annual Income both explicitly set produced the exact
same "no stable error, no navigation" result as a completely minimal baseline with
neither set — so this isn't specifically an Employment-Status-didn't-persist issue either,
at least not one visible from the client side.

## Additional corroborating evidence (2026-08-26, stress-testing follow-up)

A second, independent scenario found the same family of issue with a sharper diagnosis.
Config: Age 17, Gender Female, Occupation Code B, Business policy, Employment Status
Self-Employed, Farmers Disability cover. Generous (2-3s) settle time was inserted after
**every single field change**, and the Occupation Code and Employment Status **select
values were read directly from the DOM immediately before clicking Apply**, confirming
both were genuinely set correctly (`Occupation code value ... after Business switch: 4`
i.e. "B"; `Employment status value after settle: 1`). Age and Gender were set via the
same helper used successfully everywhere else in this suite. **Annual Income was
deliberately left unset** for this check.

Apply still produced: *"You must complete the following fields - Gender, Age Next
Birthday, Occupation/Occupation Code, Employment Status & Annual Income $"* — correctly
flagging Annual Income as missing, but **also incorrectly claiming Gender, Age Next
Birthday, Occupation/Occupation Code, and Employment Status are missing**, all four of
which were confirmed set via direct DOM read moments before. This rules out a pure
timing/race explanation (generous settle time did not help) and points instead at a
genuine validation-message-accuracy bug: the combined "must complete fields" message
appears to list some fields as missing independent of whether they're actually set,
rather than a stale read racing a slow save.

## Root cause

Unknown from black-box observation alone. Two hypotheses, neither confirmed:
1. **A genuine server-side validation block that isn't reliably reflected in the UI** —
   the transient message may be an accurate first read of a real problem, and the
   subsequent "clearing" is a client-side re-render bug that hides the error without the
   underlying block actually clearing.
2. **`isOnClientSummary()`'s detection heuristic is simply wrong for the current app** —
   its own code comment already flags it as never independently confirmed ("the URL
   doesn't reliably change and the exact heading text was never confirmed verbatim").
   It's possible Apply genuinely succeeds server-side but the client doesn't visibly
   transition the way this heuristic expects, making this a false negative rather than a
   real block. This wouldn't explain the transient error message appearing at all, though.

## Reproducibility

Confirmed across 4 independent live runs today (2026-08-26), across 3 different probe
scripts plus the original automated test failures, all agreeing: no stable visible error,
no navigation, after clicking Apply on a config that should be fully valid. The transient
error message was seen in 1 of the 2 runs that specifically polled for it early enough
(the other read errors too late in its own poll cycle to have caught it) - worth a further
run specifically timed to catch it again before concluding it's fully deterministic.

## Possible explanations to rule out first

- **A real regression** — plausible and currently the leading theory, given the
  transient-then-cleared error is a specific, reproducible signal, not silence.
- **An intentional change** — possible if "Apply" on the Illustration screen was
  deliberately changed to require an additional step not yet identified (e.g. an explicit
  Save first) before it can proceed — worth checking with a BA/PM.
- **A test artifact** — considered but doesn't fully explain the transient error message
  itself, which appeared identically across multiple different probe scripts with
  different code, including ones that never call the shared `isOnClientSummary()` helper
  at all (they check for the message text and DOM state directly).

## Suggested next step

Confirm with a BA/PM or by manual interactive testing (a real adviser, not automation)
whether Apply on this dev environment currently completes successfully at all, and if so,
what the actual success signal looks like today (URL change? Different heading text?
Something not yet captured?) — that would resolve hypothesis 2 above. If a real adviser
also can't get Apply to complete, this is a real, high-severity defect blocking the core
flow.
